paper.textual_conclusion:
The proposed XmDA method, which integrates both techniques, achieves a gain of up to 2.57 BLEU scores, 2.54 ROUGE scores and 7.13 ChrF scores. The proposed XmDA also outperforms other data augmentation techniques, e.g., Sign Back-Translation and Contrastive Transformer in Table 1, thus demonstrating the effectiveness of the proposed approach.
With the XmDA, we achieve significant improvements on two widely used sign language translation datasets: PHOENIX-2014T and CSL-Daily. Comprehensive analyses suggest that our approach improves the alignment between sign video features and gloss embeddings and the prediction of low-frequency words and the generation of long sentences, thus outperforming the compared methods in terms of BLEU, ROUGE and ChrF scores.

status.numerical_agreement_basis: 12 of 48 in-scope targets produced: the Sign Language Transformers baseline on PHOENIX-2014T (Table 1) and CSL-Daily (Table 2), with Table 10 hyperparameters, one run each at seed 56. All twelve reproduced values are higher than the published ones: PHOENIX-2014T by 1.74 (test BLEU-4) to 3.87 (test ChrF) points, CSL-Daily by 5.04 (dev ChrF) to 9.93 (dev ROUGE-L) points. The paper reports one number per cell with no seed count or variance, and this attempt ran a single seed, so there is no basis for treating these gaps as run-to-run noise; they are recorded as numerical disagreement for the reviewer to judge. CSL-Daily scoring is character-level, as in the authors' own pickle builder (code_observations), so tokenization is not the main candidate explanation. The leading hypothesis is that the paper's CSL-Daily baseline was not trained with Table 10: the released config is weaker, and the authors' fork names a CSL-Daily baseline with batch 64, dropout 0.15 and max length 30. The released-config CSL-Daily run (csl-daily-baseline-released-config-seed56, conditional evidence under gate hyperparameters) gives dev 14.30 / 42.38 / 13.91 and test 14.80 / 42.40 / 14.21 (BLEU-4 / ROUGE-L / ChrF): closer to the paper than the Table 10 run but still above it by 2.75 to 6.06 points, and it does not replace the produced values. The batch-64 / dropout-0.15 / length-30 variant named in the fork was not run. A second candidate explanation is the sign features: the authors' fork built its CSL-Daily pickles from VAC_CSLR checkpoints/cslt/gloss30check2 (Atrewin/slt concat_data.py L168-170), whereas this attempt uses SLTUNet's released SMKD checkpoint. The paper does not state its decoding setting, so greedy (beam 1) scores and the full dev grid are recorded next to the grid-selected ones. The 36 mixup/kd/xmda targets remain not_produced (protocol_ambiguous) and are never assessed for agreement.

evidence: Paper Sec. 3.1: K=4 PGEN teachers 'trained ... with varying seeds and subsets of training data'; seeds, subsets, and which 4 of the 10 teachers in Table 15 were used are not stated.

Paper Sec. 3.1: gloss embedding initialised from 'the most effective gloss-text teacher' (Table 15 ID=0, dev BLEU 27.35) and frozen. In code (model.py build_model_mixup) this is a torch state dict for signjoey GlossEmbeddings (lut + 2-layer feature_map MLP + MaskedNorm), which a fairseq PGEN teacher does not produce; the conversion is undocumented.

PGen G2T scripts call a modified fairseq (`fairseq_old`, flags --num-ref/--valid-decoding-path/--multi-bleu-path) whose train.py is not released (Atrewin/PGen issue #1, open since 2024-06-13). PGen's DA_paralle_sample is described as 'some cases' (De 30,492 pairs), not the full BT set.

Released configs/Sign_XmDA.yaml conflicts with paper Table 10: hidden 256 vs 512, 1 vs 3 layers for PHOENIX, Adam beta2 0.998 vs 0.98, label smoothing 0.0 vs 0.1, max output length 60 vs 30/50; it also mixes PHOENIX version with CSL-Daily file names and test=train pickle. No per-row configs are released.

training_XmDA.py multiplies the JSD consistency loss by 15 (L937) and an embedding 'JS' term by 15. The paper states no such factor. Recorded as published behavior, not changed.

The mix-up branch only runs when recognition_loss < 5 or randint(0,10) < 5 (L1063-1068), and _train_batch is gated by S2G_WER < 40 or randint(0,10) < 3, where S2G_WER is updated from the dev WER (L745). This is a stochastic gate the paper does not describe. Recorded, not changed.
The mix mask is gloss_predict.ge(1 - mixup_ratio) on gloss label indices, so only index 0 selects the gloss embedding. This differs from the paper's per-gloss p <= lambda rule. Recorded, not changed.

Mix-up branch (training_XmDA.py @ b6e2ca4, _train_batch L857-958 and ctc_alignment L968-1029): ctc_alignment returns label_at_pos, which holds the target gloss index of each frame inside the valid length and target[-1] as padding; it never emits the CTC blank. mix_mask_sgn = gloss_predict.ge(1 - mixup_ratio) = ge(0.4) is therefore true at every frame unless a target gloss is the silence token (index 0), so masked_select picks sign_embedding everywhere and no gloss embedding enters the encoder input. sign_embedding is recomputed by a second sgn_embed call in train mode, so the mix branch is a second dropout pass of the same features, trained with cross-entropy plus a x15 JSD consistency term against the first pass; the embedding JS term compares mix_sign_embedding with the sign_embedding it was selected from, i.e. a tensor with itself. The branch runs only when recognition_loss < 5 or random.randint(0, 10) < 5 (5/11). Net effect: a gated dropout-consistency regularizer. Recorded as evidence; not changed.

Resume semantics (training_XmDA.py @ b6e2ca4; helpers.py): (1) _save_checkpoint (L260-301) is called only on a new best dev score (L631-641), and keep_last_ckpts: 1 (configs/Sign_XmDA.yaml L63) makes ckpt_queue maxsize 1, so the run directory only ever holds the best-so-far checkpoint; there is no periodic or last-step checkpoint. (2) init_from_checkpoint (L303-359), reached via training.load_model (L208-219), restores model, optimizer and scheduler state, steps, token counts and best-score tracking. It does not restore the epoch counter, the data-iterator position, the torch/numpy/random RNG state, last_best_lr or the stop flag. (3) train_and_validate always runs for epoch_no in range(self.epochs) from 0 (L392), so a 'resumed' run trains a further full 150 epochs on top of the restored step count. (4) make_model_dir (helpers.py L26-40) deletes the run directory when overwrite: true and raises FileExistsError when false; it runs in TrainManager.__init__ (L72) before load_model, so a resume needs a new model_dir with load_model pointing at the old checkpoint. Conclusion: no real resume of an interrupted run exists without changing the epoch loop or the checkpoint policy, both behavior changes. Reloading the best checkpoint restarts from the last improvement, not from the interruption (phoenix14t-xmda-seed56 attempt 1: interrupted at step 28,000, latest checkpoint 9000.ckpt). For CSL-Daily the recovery path for an interrupted run is a full re-run: about 18 GPU-h for KD and 20 GPU-h for XmDA, and about 8 GPU-h per teacher.

torch 1.4 -> 1.7 semantics audit of signjoey @ b6e2ca4 plus patches 0001/0002 (2026-10-30, before any run in the cu110 image). Division: every torch.div call (loss.py L131, L139; training_XmDA.py L927, L937, L947, L957) is on float probability tensors. Every '/' operator is Python arithmetic or a float tensor divided by a number: loss and ppl normalisation (training_XmDA.py L1099, L1109; prediction_XmDA.py L243), throughput logging, the length penalty, attention scaling and the metrics. No integer tensor goes through '/' or torch.div, so 1.7's true division changes nothing. Floor division: '//' on tensors appears only in batch.py L291 (and the same line in patch 0001: sum(sgn_lengths) // sum(gls_lengths)) and search.py L355 (topk_ids // vocab size). Both operands are non-negative, so 1.4's integer division and 1.7's floor_divide (which truncates) give the same result. Masks: torch.where (attention.py L79, L182), masked_fill with ~mask (transformer_layers.py L75), masked_select/masked_scatter (embeddings.py L61-65; training_XmDA.py L892) and the patch 0001 masks all take masks built from comparisons (!=, ge, == 0), which are already bool in torch 1.4. No uint8 mask reaches ~, masked_* or indexing. The only uint8 tensors are the greedy-search 'finished' counters (search.py L94, L163; finished += is_eos; finished >= 1). Under 1.7's type promotion the bool-into-uint8 in-place add gives the same counts. torchtext: SignXmDA imports only torchtext.data Field, RawField, Dataset and Iterator (data.py, dataset.py, training_XmDA.py), all still in torchtext.data in 0.8.1. Conclusion: no demonstrated behavior change; nothing patched.

SLTUNet's sign_embedder MaxDecode raises a TypeError on float feat_len under PyTorch 2.11, so the extractor replaces the decoder with a no-op and computes a greedy CTC WER itself. Features are unaffected.

simple-video-utils 0.7.4 calls av.open(..., metadata_errors='replace'), and the image's PyAV 19.0.2 rejects that keyword (TypeError surfaced as 'Failed to open video' for every CSL-Daily clip). PyAV is pinned to 18.0.0, the lowest version simple-video-utils allows, which accepts it.
